title: PRD: Incident-driven circuit breakers, rollback gates, and verification for degraded serving
creator: Claire Huang
description: Background: Following the regional degradation incident in January, the postmortem identified gaps in deterministic failure isolation and insufficient automated rollback gates. This PRD defines requirements to translate postmortem actions into product and runtime features: deterministic circuit-breaker primitives in the serving runtime, explicit SLO-degradation rollback gates in the deployment control plane, Console visibility/control for operators, and a verification suite (synthetic checks + chaos tests) to validate behavior before and after rollouts. Goal: reduce blast radius and mean time to safe rollback during degraded serving by providing clear, testable, and observable controls that map directly to postmortem mitigations.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime exposes a configurable circuit-breaker API: thresholds for per-model and per-route error-rate, request-latency, and queue-depth; TTL for open state; and deterministic backoff policy.

Control plane accepts rollout policies that include two automatic rollback gates: (1) SLO degradation threshold (percent increase in 95th latency or error rate) and (2) capacity degradation threshold (sustained drop in tokens/sec for >X minutes). If either gate trips, the system must automatically initiate a safe rollback within 2 minutes.
Console shows real-time circuit-breaker state per model/route, last-triggered reason, and links to the synthetic verification run that passed/failed during the rollout.

End-to-end tests: PRs that change serving behavior must include a new synthetic verification scenario (small canonical prompt set) that runs in CI and a chaos experiment that simulates slow KV cache warmups. CI must block merging if synthetic verification fails.

Runbook: On circuit-breaker trip, runbook documented in Console and linked to incident playbook; automated checklist for on-call includes steps to mark impacted customers and to escalate to Dedicated capacity owners.
Telemetry: New metrics (circuit_breaker_open_count, cb_open_duration_seconds, rollback_initiated_by_gate) emitted to our metrics backend and visible in the SLO dashboard within 24 hours of rollout.
Rollout experiments: Canary rollouts using the new gates must demonstrate <10% false-positive rollback rate across three independent canaries before enabling global rollout.

Backward compatibility: Customers on Dedicated with pinned versions must not be impacted by default; circuit-breakers are opt-in unless higher-severity incident signatures are detected by the control plane.
decisions: Make circuit-breakers configurable at model and route granularity to balance operator control vs. simplicity.
Rollback gates are implemented in the control plane, not the runtime, to centralize cross-region decisions and provide observability.
Synthetic verification must be kept lightweight (N=25 canonical prompts) and run on the same capacity class as target rollout to avoid false confidence from mismatched hardware.
Chaos tests will be run as part of a nightly suite for major releases and as 'pre-rollout' step for any runtime or model rollout affecting >5% traffic.
Expose circuit-breaker state via both metrics and Console UI; do not rely on logs alone for operational actions.
notes: Trade-offs: Aggressive circuit-breaker thresholds reduce blast radius but increase risk of false positives; acceptance criteria include measurable false-positive targets.
We considered embedding rollback logic inside the runtime but chose control plane implementation to allow cross-model correlation and safer bulk decisions.
Need coordination with Dedicated sales and SRE to define default opt-in behavior for enterprise customers.
This work touches RBAC and audit logging; while not a hard dependency for MVP, we will require a security review before 1.0 release.
